title: Pack Calculator: choose the page structure
question: The look stays the White Sheet system. Three structures for building a packing estimate were dealt. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Builder: inputs left, estimate right
options.thesis: The estimate is the page: job, rooms and settings on the left, the line-item estimate on the right, read in dollars.
options.viewport: Page header with Quick / Photo AI switch and Calculate; a 560px input column (Job, Rooms, Settings) beside the estimate: four figures, then sections with line items and totals.
options.risk: At 1280px both columns get narrow, so Photo AI rooms (photos plus item tables) need room to breathe.

raised.raise: Changing an input after a calculation marks the estimate out of date: figures dim and an orange 'Inputs changed, recalculate' line stays until you recalculate.

options.label: Three steps on the sheet
options.thesis: Keep Details, Rooms, Review, but as one calm sheet with a small step track and the actions in one footer.
options.viewport: Page header, a small three-step track, then the current step in a 960px column (Details as property rows), Back and Next in a footer.
options.risk: The total stays hidden until the last step, so checking what a setting costs means clicking back and forth.

options.label: One page: properties, rooms, estimate
options.thesis: A Notion-style page: job facts as property rows at the top, rooms as the body, the estimate appearing below after Calculate.
options.viewport: Page title is the estimate name; under it two property columns (job, settings); then Rooms with an add bar; a sticky bottom bar carries room count and Calculate.
options.risk: A long Photo AI job pushes the estimate far down the page, so you scroll to see what changed.

options.label: Boarding pass and gate board
options.thesis: A segmented pass with tabular figures, and a board that keeps a changed row lit until noticed.
options.viewport: Rooms as board rows ranked by floor, the estimate as a segmented pass.
options.risk: A ranking board does not fit a calculator you fill in.
options.case: Estimators do not watch a ranking; they fill inputs and read a total.
options.kept: A changed input keeps the estimate marked out of date until recalculated.

options.label: Split-flap concourse board
options.thesis: Rows as live entities whose values flip in place.
options.viewport: Room rows in fixed columns with flipping figures.
options.risk: Costume on a working back-office screen.
options.case: Animated figures add noise to a money screen.
options.kept: Columns never move; recalculation changes values in place.

options.label: Orienteering map
options.thesis: A numbered course over fixed terrain, each control paired with a coded row.
options.viewport: Rooms as numbered controls along a course.
options.case: Rooms have no route between them.
options.kept: Each room row carries one coded line: floor, density, contamination.

options.label: Centre-rail reference page
options.thesis: Twin columns around one rail of keys.
options.viewport: Inputs and estimate as twin columns.
options.risk: A book page, not a tool.
options.case: Reads as an edition, not a calculator.
options.kept: One moving part: only the estimate column changes.

options.label: Vertical media feed
options.thesis: One room fills the screen, the next one snap away.
options.viewport: Each room's photos fill the viewport.
options.risk: Phone-first; this page is used at a desk.
options.case: Hides the total and the other rooms.
options.kept: Photos stay large enough to judge a room at a glance.

options.label: Transit diagram
options.thesis: Lines and interchanges as the composition.
options.viewport: Floors as lines, rooms as stations.
options.risk: Dark mural on a white-sheet product.
options.case: Breaks the product's look and adds no clarity.
options.kept: Focus one room while the others stay readable around it.
